response.sql:
WITH driver_counts AS (
    SELECT d.driverId, COUNT(q.qualifyId) AS qualifying_count
    FROM drivers AS d
    LEFT JOIN qualifying AS q ON q.driverId = d.driverId
    GROUP BY d.driverId
), average_count AS (
    SELECT AVG(qualifying_count) AS avg_qualifying_count
    FROM driver_counts
)
SELECT dc.driverId,
       dc.qualifying_count,
       1.0 * dc.qualifying_count / NULLIF(ac.avg_qualifying_count, 0) AS ratio_to_average
FROM driver_counts AS dc
CROSS JOIN average_count AS ac
ORDER BY ratio_to_average DESC, dc.driverId
LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: The average is across all drivers in the drivers table, including drivers with zero qualifying records.

alternatives.interpretation: If “average driver” means only drivers who have at least one qualifying record, calculate the average across those drivers.

WITH driver_counts AS (
    SELECT d.driverId, COUNT(q.qualifyId) AS qualifying_count
    FROM drivers AS d
    LEFT JOIN qualifying AS q ON q.driverId = d.driverId
    GROUP BY d.driverId
), average_count AS (
    SELECT AVG(qualifying_count) AS avg_qualifying_count
    FROM driver_counts
    WHERE qualifying_count > 0
)
SELECT dc.driverId,
       dc.qualifying_count,
       1.0 * dc.qualifying_count / NULLIF(ac.avg_qualifying_count, 0) AS ratio_to_average
FROM driver_counts AS dc
CROSS JOIN average_count AS ac
ORDER BY ratio_to_average DESC, dc.driverId
LIMIT 10
